summary: Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue (1856–1944) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tokyo and in Germany under Fenollosa, Fischer, Wundt, and Zeller, later serving as professor at Tokyo, Toyo University, and president of Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani (born 1939) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held multiple leadership roles, including professor and president at Komazawa University, and served as president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi (1932–2022) was a scholar of sinology, archaeology, history, and religious studies. He held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1968–1976), the University of Tsukuba (~1976–1995), and J. F. Oberlin University.

Tetsuro Watsuji (1889–1960) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Tokyo and Kyoto universities under Sōseki and Martin Heidegger, and served as professor of ethics at Kyoto (1925–1949) and Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa (1895–1989) was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1922). He held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1928–1931) and served as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).

Teun Goudriaan is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed his doctorate under Jan Gonda. He served on the faculty at Utrecht University, where he is attested as professor emeritus in 2000.

Thanissaro Bhikkhu (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin College and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1976–1986). He founded Metta Forest Monastery, where he became abbot in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in the fields of archaeology, history, and Indology. He completed studies under the guidance of Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi.

Thatchathon Attarung is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies pursuing a Ph.D. at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (2024–2026). In 2024, he served as secretary to the dean's office there and associate editor for the Journal of Applied Humanities Studies.
Theo Murray is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He is a Ph.D. candidate studying at the Australian National University.

Theodoor Paul Galestin (1907–1987) worked in archaeology, history, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom and held professorships at the University of Amsterdam (1945–1957) and Leiden University (1957–1977).

Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Boeckh, and Lachmann, earning his Ph.D. at Halle. He held professorships at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Baader (1888–1959) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his Ph.D. at Münster. He was a Privatdozent at Münster (1920) and professor of Germanic and Celtic languages at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1944).

Theodor Baunack (1861–1932) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig under Curtius and Brockhaus, earned his doctorate at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (1882–1884), and served as a teacher at the Alte Nikolaischule from 1889.

Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was a German Indologist and linguist. He completed his Ph.D. and habilitation at the University of Göttingen, where he spent his entire academic career, serving as Ordinarius professor from 1862 until 1881.

Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Windisch and Brugmann. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India (from 1900) and the University of Calcutta (~1908–1909).

Theodor Duka (1825–1908) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and St George's, University of London, later serving as an army surgeon in the Bengal Army (1854–1874) and vice-president of the British and Foreign Bible Society.

Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Peter von Bohlen, Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1851 to 1872.

Theodor Korsch (1843–1915) was a Russian linguist and Indologist who studied under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov at Moscow State University. He spent his career primarily at Moscow State University, where he became an extraordinary professor (1883–1905).
